pharm: Increases cell membrane permeability of susceptible helminths to calcium, causing rapid contraction (tetanic paralysis) of musculature and vacuolization/disintegration of the tegument, which exposes the parasite to host immune attack and allows clearance of flukes and tapeworms.

summary: Praziquantel is a broad-spectrum anthelmintic used to treat schistosomiasis (all major Schistosoma species), infections with liver and lung flukes (Clonorchis, Opisthorchis, Paragonimus), and tapeworm infections. It acts by disrupting calcium homeostasis in the parasite, causing paralysis and tegumental damage. Tablets are taken with food and swallowed whole because of an intensely bitter taste that can provoke gagging or vomiting. In neurocysticercosis (parenchymal brain cysts), drug-induced killing of CNS parasites can trigger an inflammatory reaction (headache, seizures, raised intracranial pressure), so therapy is given with corticosteroids under specialist supervision and is not used for ocular cysticercosis. It is generally well tolerated; common short-lived effects include malaise, headache, dizziness, and abdominal discomfort.
indications: Schistosomiasis due to all Schistosoma species (S. mansoni, S. haematobium, S. japonicum, S. mekongi)
Neurocysticercosis (parenchymal) - specialist use with corticosteroid cover

moa: Praziquantel rapidly increases the permeability of the helminth cell membrane to calcium ions. The resulting influx of calcium produces a marked, sustained contraction (tetanic paralysis) of the parasite musculature, dislodging flukes from their attachment sites. At slightly higher concentrations it causes vacuolization and disintegration of the schistosome tegument, exposing previously concealed parasite antigens to the host immune system and triggering phagocytic destruction. These combined effects paralyze and damage the parasite, leading to its death and clearance.

absolute: Ocular cysticercosis (parasite destruction in the eye can cause irreparable lesions)
Concurrent strong CYP enzyme inducers (e.g., rifampicin) - markedly reduce praziquantel levels
relative: Cerebral cysticercosis - treat only with corticosteroid cover and specialist supervision
Moderate to severe hepatic impairment / hepatosplenic schistosomiasis
monitor: Neurologic symptoms in (suspected) neurocysticercosis (headache, seizures, raised ICP)
Cardiac rhythm in patients with arrhythmias

preg: Animal studies have not shown teratogenicity. WHO permits the use of praziquantel during pregnancy for schistosomiasis given the morbidity of untreated infection. It may be used when the potential benefit outweighs risk; weigh treatment timing for non-urgent indications.
lact: Praziquantel is excreted in human breast milk at low concentrations. The manufacturer historically advised that women not breastfeed on the day of treatment and for 72 hours afterward; current guidance often considers it compatible. Discuss timing with the prescriber.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is established for renal impairment; praziquantel and its metabolites are largely renally excreted, so use with caution and monitor in significant impairment.
hepatic: In patients with hepatosplenic schistosomiasis (moderate to severe hepatic dysfunction, Child-Pugh B/C), reduced hepatic metabolism increases and prolongs plasma praziquantel concentrations; use with caution and consider dose reduction under monitoring.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) - substantially lower praziquantel plasma levels and may cause treatment failure; rifampicin should not be co-administered
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, cimetidine, grapefruit juice) - increase praziquantel concentrations
moderate: Dexamethasone (used in neurocysticercosis) - lowers praziquantel plasma levels
minor: Albendazole is sometimes co-administered for cysticercosis
interactions.food: Take with food; a high-carbohydrate meal increases bioavailability.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol during and shortly after treatment due to additive CNS effects.

serious: CNS inflammatory reaction in neurocysticercosis (seizures, raised intracranial pressure, encephalopathy)
emergency: New or worsening seizures or signs of raised intracranial pressure during treatment of CNS cysts

monitoring: Neurologic status during treatment of (suspected) neurocysticercosis
Cardiac rhythm in patients with arrhythmia
Resolution of infection (stool/urine egg counts as appropriate)

missed: Praziquantel is usually given as a single-day or short course. If a scheduled same-day dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered to keep doses 4-6 hours apart; if it is nearly time for the next dose, follow your prescriber's instructions rather than doubling up. For multi-day regimens, do not double a missed dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In case of overdose, give symptomatic and supportive care. A fast-acting laxative may be considered. Monitor for excessive CNS effects, and in patients with CNS cysticercosis watch for an exaggerated inflammatory reaction.
